Wow. Most people have no idea how big a deal this is. Two big things here.

  • AIs had never once beaten a professional go player in non handicap tournament conditions until last month when DeepMind went 5-0 against a professional. He was a lower tier professional than Lee Se-Dol which is what immediately led to this challenge.

Okay, that seems pretty big already but now for the mind blowing part of this:

  • This is not a "Go AI" per se. Google's Deep Mind is a generic deep learning system capable of taking on any quantifiable task. This is the same AI that was recently reported to have taught itself how to play a variety of atari video games. When I say taught itself - it uses nothing but the pixels and its score to do this. It has no idea about the rules of the game, what any shape means or anything. It teaches itself everything through deep learning. The fact this same technique can be applied to create the first AI that is comparable if not already far better than humans at one of the most complex abstract strategic games there is is... well I used to think the following patent's abstract from Google was somewhat hyperbolic and marketing oriented (even though they never really marketed this at all) :

Sapient or Sentient Artificial Intelligence

US 20140046891 A1

Abstract

A method for creating an artificial intelligence entity, specifically an artificial intelligence that is sentient and sapient is provided. The invention is capable of intelligence, human interaction, adaptive/modifiable code and thought, reasoning, learning; autonomous self-organization based on environment changes, interaction, and/or internal activity only; and other advance features. This permits a non-human, including a computer software entity, to become conscious or self-aware and interact, with the ability for sapience and understanding, as if it were human. It also has the ability to integrate with other electronic, non-electronic, or suitable devices.

Now I'm just curious what they have cooking up in private. What an exciting time we all live in. The next 10 years are going to be... interesting.
